issues.t: Brake assist can fail from water in the vacuum pump (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly feels hard and the car takes much longer to stop. A brake warning light or a loud warning tone may come on.
issues.why: Electric cars have no engine vacuum, so a small electric pump powers the brake booster. Water can get into this pump, corrode it and make it quit. Mitsubishi recalled every 2012-2017 US i-MiEV (NHTSA campaign 19V804).
issues.next: If the pedal goes hard, press much harder and pull over safely. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have the pump replaced free before driving much more.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump can stop from software or road salt (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal gets hard and stopping distances grow. A warning light and tone may come on.
issues.why: On cars built through March 2014, the pump's control software or corrosion from road salt could stop the brake vacuum pump. Dealers reprogram the controller, replace the pump or both (NHTSA campaign 14V522).
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall as well as the later pump recall. Both repairs are free.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump may fail early (recall)
issues.sym: Less brake assist, a firmer pedal and longer stops.
issues.why: Some vacuum pumps fitted to 2012 cars built December 2011 to September 2012 could fail inside. Mitsubishi replaced them under NHTSA campaign 13V031.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Several brake pump recalls cover this car, and all are free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. In a crash, the front passenger airbag inflator can burst and throw metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.why: These Takata inflators break down after years of heat and humidity. The 2012 and 2014 cars are in campaign 17V022, and the 2016-2017 cars are in campaign 17V793.
issues.next: This is urgent. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and get the free inflator replacement. Until then, keep passengers out of the front seat.

issues.t: Airbag impact sensor may delay deployment (recall)
issues.sym: The SRS airbag warning light comes on.
issues.why: Resistance can build up in the impact sensors on cars built October 2011 to September 2012. That can delay the front airbags, or stop the side and curtain airbags while the light is on (NHTSA campaign 15V594).
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the sensors replaced free. Don't ignore an airbag light on this car.

issues.t: Airbags may switch off from sensor mismatch (recall)
issues.sym: The SRS airbag warning light stays on.
issues.why: On early 2012 cars built in late 2011, some airbag sensors didn't match the system's self-check software, which could switch off the front and side airbags (NHTSA campaign 12V372).
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the sensors replaced free.

issues.t: Car won't charge, with 12-volt and power warning lights
issues.sym: The car stops charging from a normal plug, or charges for a moment and quits. The 12-volt battery light and the power system warning light come on, and the small 12-volt battery runs down.
issues.why: Capacitors inside the on-board charger can short and blow a high-voltage fuse, which also takes out the converter that keeps the 12-volt battery charged. Mitsubishi extended coverage on this charger and converter to 10 years from sale with unlimited miles.
issues.next: Don't keep trying to charge. Ask a Mitsubishi EV dealer whether the 10-year coverage still applies to your VIN. If not, ask about a rebuilt or used charger as an alternative to a new one.

issues.t: Weak 12-volt battery: won't go READY or warning lights
issues.sym: The car won't switch to READY, beeps and whistles, or lights up many warning icons, including the turtle symbol. Wipers and screens may be slow or dim.
issues.why: The small 12-volt battery powers the computers that start the car. The factory battery is a basic flooded type, and it drains if the car sits unplugged. Low voltage at start-up can confuse the car's modules.
issues.next: Test or charge the 12-volt battery first; it's the simplest fix for many warning lights. Use a battery maintainer if the car will sit more than a week, and consider a better-quality replacement.

issues.t: Driving range drops as the main battery ages
issues.sym: The car goes noticeably fewer miles on a full charge than it used to, especially in cold weather or with the heater on.
issues.why: The i-MiEV started with a small 16 kWh battery and about 62 miles of range, so any capacity loss is very noticeable. Older 2012 packs often hold far less than new. Later cars got improved cells that age better.
issues.next: Have the battery capacity read with a scan tool or at a dealer, especially before buying used. Plan trips around today's real range, and use preheating while plugged in during winter.

issues.t: Main battery won't fully charge or a cell fails
issues.sym: The battery gauge won't reach all 16 bars after a full charge, range falls sharply, or the turtle light comes on around half charge.
issues.why: A weak or failed cell inside the main lithium-ion pack. Mitsubishi extended main battery coverage to 10 years or 100,000 miles on 2012 cars when the pack can't charge to full capacity.
issues.next: Ask a Mitsubishi EV dealer to test the pack and check whether your car is still inside the battery coverage. A replacement pack outside coverage is a major repair.

issues.t: Battery gauge doesn't show fully charged
issues.sym: After a full charge, the battery gauge still doesn't show full.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued service bulletins (TSB-13-54-002 and its revision) with added troubleshooting steps for this gauge reading on 2012-2014 cars.
issues.next: Try a complete Level 2 charge and note whether it stops early. If it keeps happening, have a dealer follow the bulletin to check the battery and charger.

issues.t: Turtle mode from motor control unit fault (campaign)
issues.sym: Power drops sharply and the turtle light comes on. In the worst case the car won't start or charge.
issues.why: Some parts inside the motor control unit were not built to spec, which can make its voltage unstable. Mitsubishi ran service campaign SC-15-002 to replace the unit free.
issues.next: If power drops, move to a safe place. Ask a dealer whether SC-15-002 was completed on your VIN.

issues.t: Won't go into READY from inverter failure
issues.sym: The car won't switch to READY and can't be driven, even with a good 12-volt battery.
issues.why: A failure in the motor's power inverter (the motor control unit) can stop the car from starting. Owners report dealers taking weeks to diagnose it.
issues.next: Rule out the 12-volt battery first. Then go to a Mitsubishi EV-certified dealer or EV specialist, and ask whether any campaign or extended coverage applies.

issues.t: Won't go into READY in extreme cold
issues.sym: In very cold weather, around -13 F, the car won't switch to READY.
issues.why: The EV control relay can freeze. Mitsubishi bulletin TSB-12-54-016 introduced an improved relay.
issues.next: Park in a garage or keep the car plugged in during deep cold. If it happens, ask a dealer about the improved relay.

issues.t: Main battery cooling fan failure
issues.sym: A warning light, reduced power, or less charging speed; you may not hear the battery fan running.
issues.why: The main battery is air-cooled by a fan. Mitsubishi updated its troubleshooting for failed battery fans on 2012-2013 cars (TSB-13-54-003).
issues.next: Have a dealer read the codes and check the fan. Avoid fast charging in hot weather until it's fixed.

issues.t: Rust on battery mounting bolts and ground points (campaign)
issues.sym: Rust under the car around the main battery bolts and frame, often in salt-belt states.
issues.why: The underbody has little rust protection. Mitsubishi ran service campaign SC-14-003 to inspect and treat rust on the battery bolts and ground connections.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether SC-14-003 was done. Wash salt off the underside in winter and have the battery mounts checked before buying used.

issues.t: Won't charge on some Clipper Creek chargers (campaign)
issues.sym: Charging won't start or stops when using certain Clipper Creek home or public chargers.
issues.why: The car's EV computer software didn't communicate properly with these chargers. Mitsubishi campaign SC-13-001 updated the software.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the update was done. Try another charger to confirm the car itself charges.

issues.t: Quick charging stops or won't start
issues.sym: DC fast charging (CHAdeMO) won't start or quits after about two minutes, especially on ABB chargers.
issues.why: Software in the EV computer and battery management unit could flag a false fault with some quick chargers. Mitsubishi released reprogramming bulletins (TSB-18-54-007 and TSB-19-54-001).
issues.next: Ask a dealer to apply the software updates. Level 2 charging is not affected.

issues.t: Front seat belt frays at the recline lever
issues.sym: The front seat belt webbing looks frayed or cut near the bottom of the seat.
issues.why: The belt can get trapped under the seat recline lever, and the lever's edge rubs it. Mitsubishi's bulletin replaces the belt and fits a new lever on cars built before April 2017.
issues.next: A frayed belt may not hold in a crash. Have it replaced right away and ask a dealer about the bulletin.

issues.t: Weak or no cabin heat
issues.sym: The heater blows cool air while driving, or works only after preheating. A code B1108 may be stored.
issues.why: The car uses an electric heater to warm coolant. If the heater element weakens or isn't sensed warming up, the system shuts it off. Mitsubishi issued bulletins for the B1106 and B1108 codes.
issues.next: Check the coolant level first. Have a shop read the A/C and heater codes; a failing heater unit usually has to be replaced. Clear frost from the windows before driving.

issues.t: Air conditioning stops working
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air or won't turn on.
issues.why: Owners report failures of the electric A/C unit on 2012 cars. The system is also used to cool the battery during fast charging, so a fault matters beyond comfort.
issues.next: Get an A/C diagnosis before deciding on repairs; electric compressor work can be a big job.

issues.t: Heated seat stops working
issues.sym: One of the heated seats no longer warms up.
issues.why: Owners report the seat heater element or its controls failing.
issues.next: Check the fuse first, then have the seat heater tested.
